trees.name: Red River Gum of the Celia Mendez Garden
trees.note: The thickest trunk in the whole municipal catalogue at 4.86m girth and 34.8m tall, a relict of the riverside market gardens. Undated, no photo, peripheral neighbourhood 3km east, and no story beyond size. Strong candidate the day Cordoba grows past seven.

trees.name: Ash of Santa Marina
trees.note: Two sources and real history (documented in Los Arboles de Cordoba, 1984, and the 2002 provincial inventory; local botanist Rafa Tamajon argues it is centenarian). But only 9.5m tall with visible trunk decay and declining. Latitude was lost in the catalogue PDF extraction and needs recovering from the page image.

trees.name: Chinaberry at the Puerta de Almodovar
trees.note: 24.5m tall casting 400 square metres of shade, about 72 years old now. Handsome, young, no story yet.

trees.name: Cypress at the Alcazar entrance
trees.note: 26.5m tall on a crown only 3.5m wide, a green needle, and free to see outside the ticket gate. About 77 years old, so young for us, but visually the most striking of Cordoba's modern trees.

trees.name: Stone Pine of Santa Maria de Trassierra
trees.note: 3.26m girth, 25m, roughly 90 years. Reachable by Aucorsa line L-T in about 19 minutes but only about five services a day, which strains the day-trip boundary.

trees.name: Photinia at the Palacio de la Merced
trees.note: A naturalists' walk claims it is the oldest specimen of its species in the province. Not in the municipal catalogue and unverified. One follow-up search would settle it.

trees.name: Casuarinas of the Plaza de Jeronimo Paez
trees.note: Three trees, the tallest above 30m, five minutes from the Mezquita. Single-sourced to the municipal catalogue with no independent second source and no published age.

trees.name: Himalayan Cedar of the Plaza del Cardenal Toledo
trees.note: 22.5m and the near-sole occupant of its square, about 102 years old, and it predates the 1945 garden around it. Single-sourced, no photo.

trees.name: Siberian Elm of the Alcazar
trees.note: 27m against a species maximum of 15m, genuinely exceptional. Single-sourced and behind a paid gate, though the gardens are free on summer mornings.

trees.name: Canary Palm of the Doctor Emilio Luque Square
trees.note: Around 112 years and among the oldest palms in the city. Single-sourced, and the catalogue names red palm weevil as the threat that has killed dozens of Cordoba's Canary palms, so survival needs checking before anything is published.

trees.name: Ginkgo of the Agriculture Gardens
trees.note: About 72 years, the oldest ginkgo in Cordoba's public gardens and a landmark for the city's botany students. Young, and no photo.

trees.name: Olive of the Agriculture Gardens
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Looks perfect on paper at 2.6m girth, and it is the tree the naturalists' walk stops at, but the municipal catalogue itself says it has barely any history: it was installed on 30 April 2009, transplanted from Castellon. An old tree in the wrong city. This is the trap in Cordoba olive research; do not confuse it with the Patio de los Naranjos olive.

trees.name: The private patios of the Patios Festival
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as ordinary entries. UNESCO-listed and full of old citrus, but open only during the May festival. Hard rule 10 restricted access; if ever used, the restriction must be stated in the entry itself.

trees.name: Sotos de la Albolafia
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A protected Natural Monument of 21 hectares of riverside woodland between the Roman and San Rafael bridges. No single identifiable tree and no trunk to stand at, so it fails the collectible-point test exactly as a long avenue does.

trees.name: Hackberries of Santa Maria de Trassierra
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Base girths to 5.97m, but condition rated bad to very bad, systematically pollarded, and built into the boundary walls of private houses. Private-land risk with no viewing point.

trees.name: Molle and swamp cypress of Cordoba Zoo
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Inside a paid zoo, and the molle stands inside a gibbon enclosure.

trees.name: Pecan of El Arenal
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. On a fenced empty lot.

trees.name: Tetraclinis of the Patio de los Naranjos
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Recorded as disappeared.

trees.name: Sakamoto no Mukunoki
trees.note: Dazaifu city designation 2015, 25.5m tall, 3.65m girth, roots exposed and spreading seven metres, and it has a full street address (Sakamoto 3-268-1), which makes it the most precisely placeable untouched tree in the region. One more pass would ship it.

trees.name: The Great Yamamomo of Kanetake
trees.note: Prefectural designation, 4.7m girth, individually mapped. Nishi ward, needs a second source and a photo.

trees.name: The Camphor of Shimizu
trees.note: 9.7m girth in Minami ward, which would be among the city's largest. No coordinate, no second source yet.

trees.name: The Married Camphors and Great Ginkgo of Torikai Hachimangu
trees.note: Two individually mapped trees at one shrine, so pins exist, but no age, no measurements and no open-licence photograph of either.

trees.name: Hibaru Sakura
trees.note: Thirteen cherries, so it fails the collectible-point test as a city entry, but the story is one of the best in Fukuoka: in 1984 someone tied a tanka to a trunk to protest the felling, the mayor replied in verse and the plan was dropped. Belongs in a collection rather than on the city page. Also unresolved whether all eight originals still live.

trees.name: The Camphor of Hakozaki-gu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP without a current on-site check. The city's largest at 11.4m girth and 800 years claimed, but a March 2025 surveyor wrote that he could not tell whether it is still alive: trunk and branches so smothered by a climbing fig that no camphor foliage is visible, severe hollowing, front roots dead, vigour rated two out of five.

trees.name: Hakomatsu of Hakozaki-gu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. The present pine is a replacement of unknown generation. Context inside another story at most.

trees.name: Kankakeshii of Kashii-gu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Kaibara Ekiken already recorded in the Edo period that the tree standing then had been grown from the old one's seed. Alive and visitable, but only ever a footnote.

trees.name: Tenjin no Mori, Dazaifu
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A prefectural designation covering 51 camphors across the grounds. Story material for the great camphor, not an entry.

trees.name: Tachibanayama camphor primeval forest
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A special natural monument of roughly 3,000 camphors. Only the named Tachibanayama Great Camphor inside it could qualify, and that needs a bus plus a 40 minute climb.

trees.name: The Chokushi-michi camphor avenue, Kashii
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Saplings donated and planted in 1926, so about a century old, and an avenue.

trees.name: The Hobashira-seki of Najima
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A fossilised trunk.

trees.name: The Chishanoki of Komyozen-ji
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as visitable. The temple has been closed to the public since 2018 for precinct works with no confirmed reopening.

trees.name: The Mukunoki of Kouun Shrine, Nishi Park
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as told. Presented locally as the tree that survived the 1945 air raid, but no age, no measurements and only tourism blogs, and part of it was cut back around 2021 as a breakage risk. Note for the whole city: there is no Fukuoka equivalent of the Hiroshima survivor-tree registry, so no Fukuoka tree may be given an air-raid survival story.

trees.name: The Choja no Fuji of Musashi-ji
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A wisteria vine, and about 45 minutes out.

trees.name: Milestone Hackberry of the Todai-ji West Gate
trees.note: 3.95m girth and 30m, the tallest tree in the official Nara Park giant-tree course, believed to mark the milestone on the Kyoto road that begins at Todai-ji's Tegai-mon. Age explicitly not recorded, single official source, and no coordinate exists for the West Gate ruins in any gazetteer. Needs a pin before it can ship.

trees.name: Roben-sugi at Nigatsu-do
trees.note: Superb legend: the infant Roben was said to have been carried off by an eagle and left in its branches, and Todai-ji's founding abbot was reunited with his mother beneath it. But the original fell to a typhoon in 1961 and the present tree is a successor, roughly 60 years old. Includable only on the Kyoto Gion-cherry precedent, and only if the entry says plainly it is a replanting. Good open photos

trees.name: Wakamiya Great Camphor, Kasuga Taisha
trees.note: Legend says Empress Jingu planted it. Sources contradict badly on size: 12.46m girth and 24m in one record against '8m+, 7m tall, three trees planted together' in another, which is not a rounding difference. No official register lists it, and the one open photo fails the card crop with stone lanterns filling the centre.

trees.name: Great Zelkova of Kasuga
trees.note: 4.9m girth, the largest zelkova in Nara Park, hollow and mossy. Single-sourced to the shrine's own forest-walk page, no coordinate, no age, and 'upper portions lost' needs checking that it is thriving rather than a relic.

trees.name: Cycad of Jokyo-ji
trees.note: Nara City Natural Monument, 1979, and close to the station. Small tree at a minor temple, thin sourcing, visitor access unverified.

trees.name: Bayberry of Oryu-ji
trees.note: Nara City Natural Monument, 1979. Same profile as the cycad: real designation, thin sourcing, access unverified.

trees.name: Persimmon of Jigen-ji
trees.note: Nara City Natural Monument, 1983. Real designation, thin sourcing, access unverified.

trees.name: Ichiigashi of the Kasugayama primeval forest
trees.note: 6.00m girth and 35m on the southern path, which would be a strong entry, but one source and no coordinate. A single named tree inside the forest can qualify even though the forest cannot.

trees.name: Yogo-no-Matsu, Kasuga Taisha
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. The original pine died in 1995; a successor sapling grows beside the surviving stump. Famous as the claimed origin of the pine painted on every Noh stage, though even that attribution is disputed as a later invention.

trees.name: Chisokuin Nara-no-Yaezakura
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. The tree designated a national Natural Monument in 1923 has died; today's cherries are propagated descendants. Chisokuin is a closed sub-temple open roughly one day a year.

trees.name: Kasugayama Primeval Forest
trees.note: NEVER SHIP as one entry. A Special Natural Monument covering a whole mountain, with no single tree and nowhere to stand. A named individual inside it can qualify separately.

trees.name: Kasuga Ichiigashi giant-tree group
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. Thirty-plus separate trees over 3m girth scattered across the precinct, designated as a group. No single destination.

trees.name: Sunazuri-no-Fuji
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A wisteria vine on a trellis.

trees.name: Shoryaku-ji Kojii grove
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A prefecturally designated grove rather than one tree, and Bodaisen-cho is well beyond the day-trip boundary.

trees.name: Takiyama left-spiral Torreya
trees.note: NEVER SHIP for Nara. A prefectural Natural Monument, but in Tsuge-Hayama-cho, inside the municipal boundary only through a merger and far over 30 minutes out.

trees.name: Tsukigase Oyama ancient plums
trees.reason: out of range, and an ensemble
trees.note: NEVER SHIP for Nara. City-designated in March 2026, but Tsukigase is roughly an hour out, and it is a group rather than one tree.

trees.name: The thousand-year cedar at the Kasuga Treasure Hall cafe
trees.note: NEVER SHIP. A cut stump on indoor display. Easy to confuse with the living great cedar, which is why it is recorded here.
